subject.title: Reject split outbound agent session ownership

question: Should Gateway `send` permanently support separately owned control and transcript sessions through `requesterSessionKey` and `mirrorAgentId`, or should this repair remain a narrow rejection of contradictory legacy `agentId`/`sessionKey` requests?
rationale: The reported bug supports rejecting an inconsistent owner/session pair, but it does not by itself establish a public need for a new pairwise ownership API that permits different valid owners within one send operation.

options.title: Keep a narrow ownership guard
options.body: Remove the new pairwise protocol surface and reject mismatched legacy owner/session requests consistently at Gateway and lower outbound boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor the pairwise protocol
options.body: Accept the two new public fields as a supported Gateway contract, then require exact-head compatibility and live behavior proof for both legacy and independent-pair requests.

options.title: Pause the expansion
options.body: Keep the hardening direction pending until an owner can provide a concrete supported use case for separately owned control and transcript sessions.

recommendation.title: Keep a narrow ownership guard
recommendation.body: Remove the new pairwise protocol surface and reject mismatched legacy owner/session requests consistently at Gateway and lower outbound boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: History connects this contributor to the consolidation of outbound session context and Gateway agent propagation that define the affected ownership contract.
